issues.text: On Payment with Alice (Standard) and Bob (Student), applying TEAM15 shows “That promo code is not recognised.” and retains subtotal $165.00, discount −$0.00, total due $165.00, rather than the expecte

Confirming a completed one-attendee registration opens a confirmation message containing the attendee count, organisation, reserved seats, and the same total due. — After the recorded Confirm registration click in step 10, the observed surface was still Payment with 1 attendee and a $120.00 total; no confirmation message or its required details were observed.

For Alice on Standard ($120) plus Bob on Student ($45), applying TEAM15 shows the reconciled $165.00 subtotal, $24.75 discount, and $140.25 total due. — Steps 24-25 show Alice · standard and Bob · student, which reconcile to the displayed $165.00 subtotal, but after Apply with TEAM15 the observed discount remained −$0.00 and total due remained $165.00 rather than $24.75 and $140.25.

Valid promo code TEAM15 is rejected on Payment: immediately after Apply, visible error says “That promo code is not recognised.” and the summary remains Discount −$0.00 and Total due $260.00 for a $26
Contact accepts the punctuation-only phone value -------: clicking Continue advanced to Attendees rather than remaining on Contact with a visible phone validation error.

Applying TEAM15 to Alice Standard and Bob Workshop deducts exactly 15% of the $380.00 subtotal and reconciles Total due. — The two attendees and $380.00 subtotal were observed (steps 50-51), but applying TEAM15 produced “That promo code is not recognised,” Discount −$0.00, and Total due $380.00 (step 52), rather than a $57.00 discount and $323.00 total.

Seats outside 1–12 are blocked on Attendees, and punctuation-only phone input is blocked on Contact. — Both 13 and 0 seats kept the wizard on Attendees with “Seats reserved must be between 1 and 12.” (steps 29 and 31), but submitting phone ------- advanced to Attendees instead of remaining on Contact with a phone error (steps 33-34).
Navigating to http://localhost:4121/bookflow/account.html returns a 404 Error response with "Message: File not found." instead of the account settings screen.

The requested /bookflow/account.html account-settings route opens successfully after saving. — Step 15 navigated to http://localhost:4121/bookflow/account.html, and step 16 records that the route failed and remained on a verified 404 response.
Required-name validation feedback does not clear when the Full name is corrected: "Full name is required." remains visible after entering "Alex Rivera".
Duplicate-click/submission protection failed: after the initial confirmed order BK-1001, the further Place order activation produced a second confirmed order BK-1002 and a second $1002.90 receipt for

Rapid/repeated Place order clicks create exactly one confirmation and one receipt, preventing duplicate orders. — After a valid submission from the empty-receipt state, step 18 observes one confirmation and one receipt, but the final snapshot in step 20 explicitly confirms that two receipts are visible and duplicate-order status is displayed.
Rapid repeated submission creates two receipts (BK-1001 and BK-1002), not the intended exactly one receipt.

Clicking Place order with valid details immediately shows processing feedback and visibly disables or otherwise prevents activation of Place order. — Step 1 clicked Place order to inspect the interim state, but the trace records no resulting processing indicator, disabled button state, DOM change, or other observed effect.

Two rapid Place order clicks on a fresh valid checkout create exactly one receipt. — The first click completed as BK-1001, and step 10 explicitly observed two receipts, BK-1001 and BK-1002, after the duplicate-submission check.
Bulk close updated both intended rows to Closed but reported closing only 1 ticket in its toast instead of 2.

Clicking Close selected closes the selected tickets, clears the selection, and shows the requested closure toast. — Step 5 directly clicked Close selected but recorded domChanged=NO; the post-action observation still showed Invoice total looks wrong and Export never finishes selected, “2 selected,” and Close selected enabled, with no recorded close result or toast.
Table columns reflow horizontally when search reduces rows, shifting headers and cell alignment between states.

Enabling Open only removes closed tickets and shows a count equal to the remaining open rows. — After the Open only control was clicked in step 8, the recorded table still showed all eight tickets and explicitly noted the first ticket was Closed, rather than removing the closed ticket.

Clicking Send to stakeholders shows a visible completion response. — Step 3 directly clicked Send to stakeholders and recorded domChanged=NO; the final observation explicitly states that sending was exercised but showed no visible completion response.

Clicking Export CSV shows a visible export confirmation without navigating away. — Export CSV was clicked in step 2, and the immediate subsequent observation in step 3 says it produced no visible confirmation or dismissal control; the URL remained /report.html and the page was unchanged.

Clicking Send to stakeholders shows its corresponding visible confirmation without navigating away. — Send to stakeholders was directly clicked in step 3 with domChanged=NO, and no resulting confirmation, navigation, or other observed effect was recorded.
Booking row interprets the Assign to value Injected as markup: it renders bold Injected instead of displaying the literal tag text, demonstrating unsafe markup rendering.

Booking 15 August 2026 with Injected preserves the entire entered name as literal text in the booking row, without formatting or losing markup characters. — The input is observed literally as `Injected` in step 8, but the resulting sole row in steps 10-11 is `Sat, 15 Aug 2026 — Injected`, so the `` tags were stripped and the displayed booking data was corrupted.

Submitting Book shift with no selected shift date shows a visible required-date error and leaves the booking area at No shifts booked. — After the no-date submission, step 10 observes an empty date control but an existing booking row, and step 11 freshly confirms the sole row `Sat, 15 Aug 2026 — Injected`; therefore the booking area does not remain `No shifts booked`.
Undo restores Cable to 18 and removes its receipt, but leaves stale error “Only 21 ... on hand.”
Quantity spinbutton has no accessible name despite its visible “Quantity” label.

Undoing the latest Panel A3 shipment restores Panel to 11 and leaves only its earlier received movement in Panel's history, with the requested movement total of 1. — Step 23 shows Undo restored Panel A3 to 11 and removed the latest Panel shipment, but the screen still showed 3 total movements rather than the expected 1 because the earlier Washer receipt and Screw shipment remained in history.

Undoing the last successful Cable receipt after an over-shipment error clears the error, restores Cable to 18, and removes the receipt from history. — Step 52 directly clicked Undo last, but it had domChanged=NO and no post-Undo state was observed; the recorded screen still showed the error and Cable at 21 with 7 movements, rather than the required cleared error, Cable 18, and no remaining Cable movement.
Quantity spinbutton has no accessible name despite the visible Quantity label.
The submission dialog does not dismiss when its backdrop is clicked. A fresh re-check showed “Audit submitted” still visible over the dimmed audit table after clicking outside it.
Each count stepper is exposed only as “−” or “+”, with no accessible item/action name.

The submission dialog can be dismissed by Close, backdrop click, and Escape, revealing the audit table each time. — Close hid the dialog and Escape later revealed the table (steps 3 and 6 observations), but after the backdrop click the dialog remained visible on a fresh check (step 5).

Non-first-row Washer 11mm controls affect Washer, allowing its count to reach 58 with variance -2 while other rows remain unchanged. — Several attempted Washer-minus activations instead changed Hex bolt M4 while Washer stayed 60 (steps 7, 9, 11, 16, 18, 25, 27, and 29); one direct Washer action reached 59/-1 (step 22), but the required second action did not produce 58/-2 and the observed state instead included Hex at 139/-1 (step 2
Stepper controls expose only “−” and “+” names, not the affected item or action.

Increasing CBL-2M twice from its System/initial count of 18 results in System 18, Counted 20, and Variance +2. — After repeated attempted CBL-2M plus clicks, steps 12-14 still record CBL-2M as System 18, Counted 18, Variance —, while the clicks instead changed WSH-11.
